ARTEFACT: Movable archaeological finds, portable object-like remains, and groups of finds recovered in archaeological contexts. This includes jewellery, tools, pottery and ceramic assemblages, architectural members when treated as finds, bones, ash, tiles, fragments, and other deposited remains. Include essential modifiers or complements when they form part of the object description. Examples: «ενώτια», «αναθηματική στήλη», «κινητά ευρήματα», «αιχμές βελών», «κόσμημα», «θραύσμα». Do not annotate immovable structures such as tombs, walls, temples, wells, altars, stoas, rooms, or sanctuaries as ARTEFACT.
PERIOD: Archaeological periods, chronological phases, cultural phases, and ancient date ranges. Include the full chronological expression, including prepositions or modifiers when they are part of a dating or phase expression. Examples: «Νεολιθική εποχή», «Τελική Νεολιθική», «ΥΕ ΙΙΙΒ/Γ», «από το 3600 ως το 3000 π.Χ.», «2ος αι. π.Χ.». Exclude modern dates, excavation seasons, publication years, and modern historical references such as «2019».
LOCATION: Named geographical places and place names, including cities, villages, regions, countries, islands, bays, rivers, ancient place names, museums, cultural institutions, universities, and named archaeological sites when used as toponyms rather than structures. Examples: «Πλωτινόπολη», «ἀρχαῖο Μολύκρειον», «Ραμνοῦς», «Λαδοχώρι», «Φιγάλεια», «όρμος του Αγίου Ιωάννη», «Αρχαιολογικό Μουσείο Ιωαννίνων». Do not annotate archaeological structures such as temples, sanctuaries, stoas, agoras, acropoleis, or cemeteries as LOCATION, unless the expression functions primarily as a place name. Exclude personal names of archaeologists, researchers, authors, and excavators.
CONTEXT: Immovable archaeological contexts, stratigraphic units, built spaces, architectural structures, named monuments, and in situ parts of structures. This includes temples, sanctuaries, wells, tombs, altars, stoas, agoras, acropoleis, cemeteries, deposits, and structural architectural members when they are part of a building or monument. Examples: «πηγάδι», «χείλος», «καμαροσκέπαστος θάλαμος», «ἀποθέτης», «αγροικία», «Ιερό του Πανός», «θεμέλια τοίχου», «δάπεδα τῶν οἰκιῶν», «παραστάδες». Prefer the complete meaningful structure span, especially named monuments, sanctuaries, and coordinated structure names. When divine or personal names are part of a named sanctuary, temple, or monument, annotate the full structure as CONTEXT rather than the name separately as PERSON. Do not annotate named geographical places as CONTEXT. Do not annotate loose fragments, portable finds, ash, bones, ceramics, tiles, or general natural surfaces such as «έδαφος» as CONTEXT unless they denote an in situ archaeological layer or structure.
MATERIAL: Specific materials, rocks, minerals, clays, metals, pigments, shells, compounds, and material adjectives from which artefacts, finds, or structures are made. Examples: «μάρμαρο», «άργιλος», «χαλκός», «οστέινος», «μαλαχίτης». Annotate material adjectives separately from artefacts when they simply indicate material, e.g. «πήλινη» + «σφραγίδα». Do not annotate broad generic expressions such as «πρώτες ύλες» unless a specific material is named. If bones, ash, ceramics, tiles, or fragments are described as deposited finds rather than as the substance of another object, annotate them as ARTEFACT instead of MATERIAL.
SPECIES: Animal and plant species, including real and mythological animals when they denote living beings or depicted creatures. Include parenthetical or synonymous species terms when present. Examples: «αγελάδα», «μοσχαράκι», «λιοντάρι», «σκύμνος», «φίδι», «γρύπας». If the animal or plant term denotes the material of an object, such as shell, bone, ivory, or wood used as material, annotate it as MATERIAL instead of SPECIES.
PERSON: Historical, mythological, divine, or legendary figures mentioned as persons or named beings. Examples: «Αλέξανδρος», «Αλέξανδρος ο Μέγας», «Απόλλων», «Κυβέλη», «Σφίγγα». Include inflected forms such as «Αλεξάνδρου» or «Ποσειδώνα». Exclude modern archaeologists, researchers, authors, excavators, and scholars. Do not annotate personal or divine names separately when they are part of a named sanctuary, temple, or monument. Do not annotate personal names as LOCATION or CONTEXT.
FEATURE: Stylistic, typological, iconographic, decorative, technical, morphological, or type characteristics of artefacts, figures, structures, or artistic representations. Examples: «κιβωτιόσχημος», «αδιακόσμητη», «διακοσμημένη», «ερυθρόμορφο», «ανάγλυφη διακόσμηση», «ένθρονη μορφή», «ανθρωπόμορφα», «ζωόμορφα». Do not annotate materials, periods, place names, persons, abstract narrative terms, isolated generic adjectives, or architectural members themselves as FEATURE. Do not annotate complete object names as FEATURE only because they contain descriptive, decorative, or typological modifiers.
